title: Global status value, increment, decrement, and highwater primitives

scope.rationale: These are the complete status.c state identities and four lock-assuming primitives used directly by the global allocation core. Manager now uses the source ten-slot current/highwater model rather than allocator-specific counters.
excluded_responsibilities: sqlite3_status/sqlite3_status64 public locking and reset APIs

external_source_responsibilities: Caller ownership of the allocator or pcache status mutex selected by statMutex
dependencies.caller_closure: The four internal primitives and their complete ten-slot state are assigned. Public query locking and non-allocator producer integration remain separate units.

inputs: Status operation 0 through 9 and signed update/highwater amount under the source preconditions
outputs: Current value or updated current/highwater slot
contracts.ownership: Process-lifetime status slots own no allocations.
contracts.state_and_results: Up accepts signed deltas and raises highwater only when current exceeds it; Down requires nonnegative N and leaves highwater unchanged; Highwater accepts only size/parser operations and never changes current.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: Caller holds the mutex selected by the source statMutex table. No callbacks or I/O.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: No result-code failure path; invalid operations violate source assertions/preconditions.

representation_differences: The private C sqlite3Stat object is embedded in memory.Manager as two exact ten-element i64 arrays.
The active 64-bit profile makes sqlite3StatValueType i64.
Manager selects its allocator STATIC_MEM handle for allocator slots and the Lifecycle-provided STATIC_PMEM/PCACHE1 handle for page-cache slots, matching statMutex topology.
C writable-static-data macros collapse to direct Manager field access because SQLITE_OMIT_WSD is absent.

oracle.protocol: Native primitive tests exercise increment, decrement, independent slots, highwater-only updates, and reset queries. The infrastructure C/Zig differential compares allocator status current/highwater/count/size observations and shuffled process lifecycle cases.
oracle.normalization: Private global/Manager addresses and mutex identity are ignored; operation indices and all numeric state transitions are exact.

assurance.oom: No allocation and no OOM path.
assurance.io_crash_concurrency: No I/O. Allocator and page-cache slots use distinct source-corresponding mutex identities; concurrent status differential remains open.
assurance.malformed_input: Invalid operations are source-precondition violations; all ten valid slots are representable.
assurance.continuation: Updates are deterministic and subsequent reads continue from exact state.
assurance.performance: Constant-time indexed updates; Manager embedding adds no allocation.

integration.production_owner: src/core/memory.zig Manager status arrays and primitives
integration.native_call_path: Manager allocator paths use statusValue/Up/Down/Highwater directly; public status queries use Manager.status.
integration.bounded_owner_retired: The prior separate allocator-specific current/highwater fields were removed.

independent_review.notes: Must independently verify all source assertions, ten-slot transitions, target-width choice, cross-subsystem lock topology, and concurrency.

known_blockers: Allocator and page-cache producers share the status owner with source-corresponding lock selection; exact concurrent event evidence remains pending.
